text:
Priya K: heads up — ran the long-context soak (1M token synthetic) against the kv-cache build from last week and seeing linear mem growth + degraded p50 after ~20k steps. suspect fragmentation + allocator churn, not leak. :thinking:

Leo H: can you paste the pmap/top output? is it all in the runtime process or helpers?

Priya K: all in runtime. here's the lightweight snapshot from the run:```
PID  1234 VmRSS: 12.8G  (start)
PID  1234 VmRSS: 16.3G  (after 100k tokens)
heap: kv-cache arenas: 92 active blocks, hole map rising
alloc histogram: small-block bins (64/128/256) showing high churn
```

Samir: that looks like micro-fragmentation. allocator is handing out lots of 128B/256B chunks then never coalescing because of long-lived KV entries and variable delete patterns.

Marta R: do we have the slab metadata counters enabled for that run? would like to see per-slab free/used distribution.

Priya K: yes — exported slab counters to prometheus. quick paste:```
kv.slab.64.free: 120
kv.slab.64.used: 2110
kv.slab.128.free: 32
kv.slab.128.used: 4200
kv.slab.256.free: 5
kv.slab.256.used: 3140
kv.coalesce.ops: 3
kv.compact.scan_rate: 0.002
```

Leo H: coalesce.ops only 3 — compactor effectively idle. we throttle compaction aggressively to avoid CPU spikes, but that can let fragmentation accumulate.

Devon: maybe the compactor threshold is too conservative for long-context workloads. propose: increase scan_rate temporarily for long-context mode or add an adaptive backoff based on free-ratio.

Samir: agree. another angle: change block size mix — shift some allocation pressure from 128B to 256B to reduce adjacency holes. But that increases internal slack. tradeoffs.

Priya K: tried a quick A/B on dev env: bumping default 128->192 (mixed bin) reduced hole count by ~30% and p50 improved 8%, but peak RSS up by ~6% — cost vs latency trade.

Marta R: can we instrument reuse distance and eviction churn? want to see if pages are getting re-pinned frequently which prevents coalescing.

Priya K: added sampling (1/1000 ops) and saw many entries with reuse distance < 50ms during bursts, then long tails where entries persist for minutes. pattern: hot prefix churn + very long-lived tails -> slabs end up fragmented.

Infra Bot: note recorded: "kv-long-context-soak-5409871234" uploaded to perf-bucket with pprof and counter dumps.

Leo H: interesting — hot churn prevents background compactor from getting contiguous free runs. two proposals: (A) opportunistic compaction during low-syscalls (cheap coalesce), (B) micro-migration of small survivors into a compact slab epoch to free up contiguous ranges.

Samir: (A) is low-risk — implement a cooperative coalesce hook that runs when tail-latency < SLO and CPU headroom exists. (B) more invasive: copy survivors, update pointers, requires careful KV pointer swap and epoch fencing.

Priya K: what's ETA for (A)? can it be a quick feature flag to test in canary?

Leo H: I can have a PR by EOD that exposes adaptive_coalesce_rate and a simple hint: if free_ratio < 0.15 and cpu_idle > 20% then increase scan_rate x4. feature flag gated.

Marta R: add a metric for compactor pause time + bytes_moved so we can correlate with latency spikes.

Devon: also think about allocator heuristics: a small fast path to prefer reusing recently-freed microblocks from same slab stripe to reduce cross-slab fragmentation. cheap LRU per-slab.

Samir: yeah but beware of contention if we add per-slab LRU. maybe per-core caches with periodic global reconcile.

Priya K: next steps: Leo will add adaptive_coalesce flag + metrics, Samir will prototype biased block-size allocation in a branch, Marta will add reuse-distance histogram to the exporter, I'll run the long-context soak again and post results.

Leo H: ping me once soak starts — I'll watch compactor metrics and adjust thresholds. :eyes:

Priya K: thanks — saving perf traces now, will attach when done.

Devon: long-term, we should consider a compaction window scheduled between model batches (kernel selection intervals) — we already have quiet periods when batching shifts. tie compaction to batching heuristics.

Priya K: good call — will add to roadmap item: "kv compaction tied to batching quiet windows".

Infra Bot: reminder: canary rollout policy requires 2 green runs for adaptive flags before ramp.

Marta R: thanks all — this feels actionable. I'll start a short RFC summarizing the two approaches and perf targets. :+1:
